finding.claim: LRUCache.set deletes an existing key but never re-inserts it, so updating a cached key loses the entry and a subsequent get returns undefined.
finding.title: LRUCache.set drops update for existing key

verifier.reason: The code at internal/lrucache.js:26 deletes the existing key and the re-insertion at internal/lrucache.js:35 is guarded by !deleted at internal/lrucache.js:28, so updating an existing key removes it without re-inserting and get at internal/lrucache.js:10-12 returns undefined.

repro.testCode:
import assert from 'node:assert/strict'
import LRUCache from './internal/lrucache.js'

const cache = new LRUCache()
cache.set('a', 1)
assert.equal(cache.get('a'), 1)
cache.set('a', 2)
assert.equal(cache.get('a'), 2)
cache.set('b', 10)
cache.set('b', 20)
assert.equal(cache.get('b'), 20)
assert.equal(cache.get('a'), 2)
repro.expectedBehavior: LRUCache.set on an existing key updates its value, so a subsequent get returns the new value instead of undefined.
repro.rationale: The buggy set() deletes an existing key and only re-inserts when delete returned false, so updating a key removes it. Setting 'a' to 1 then to 2 and asserting get('a') === 2 fails on the buggy code (returns undefined) and passes when fixed.

finding.claim: When cloning a SemVer instance with different loose/includePrerelease options the code re-parses version.version which excludes build metadata, so build identifiers are silently lost.
finding.title: SemVer re-parse from SemVer loses build metadata

verifier.reason: The constructor at classes/semver.js:34 reassigns version to version.version when options differ, then re-parses that string at classes/semver.js:53 and derives build only from regex group m[5] at classes/semver.js:93, so a SemVer whose version string excludes build metadata loses its build identifiers.
